ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a single-loop RLC series circuit. On the left side is a sinusoidal voltage source; an upper section is, in sequence, a 4Ω resistor and a 1H inductor, labeled with voltage V1, indicating that V1 is connected across the two ends of these two series elements. The right vertical branch is, in sequence, a 5Ω resistor and a 1/36 F capacitor, labeled with voltage V2, indicating that V2 is connected across the two ends of these two series elements. The problem gives the excitation as 100 cos(3t) V, therefore the angular frequency is ω=3 rad/s. Reasoning: Since the 4Ω+1H part where V1 is located and the 5Ω+1/36F part where V2 is located are in the same series loop, the current amplitude flowing through the two is the same, so the ratio of voltage amplitudes is equal to the ratio of the corresponding impedance magnitudes. The impedance of the V1 part is Z1=4+jωL=4+j3, so |Z1|=sqrt(4^2+3^2)=5. The impedance of the V2 part is Z2=5+1/(jωC)=5+1/(j·3·1/36)=5-j12, so |Z2|=sqrt(5^2+12^2)=13. Therefore amplitude(V2)/amplitude(V1)=|Z2|/|Z1|=13/5=2.6.
